newsitem.title: USA: USX-Delhi loss cut by depreciation change.
newsitem.headline: USX-Delhi loss cut by depreciation change.

text.p: USX-Delhi Group reported a second quarter loss of $1.5 million, or $0.16 per share, after a favorable depreciation adjustment related to the first quarter, compared to a loss of $1.2 million, or $0.12 per share, a year earlier.
It said the favorable aftertax effect of this special item was $1.1 million, resulting in a year-to-date favorable depreciation adjustment recorded in second quarter of $2.1 million aftertax.

This adjustment resulted from revisions in the economic lives of Delhi's pipeline systems and gas processing plants, the company explained. The expansion of these operating assets during the past two years, along with the addition of dedicated reserves, has extended their economic useful lives.
It said this change will have a favorable effect on depreciation expense in future periods.

Second quarter 1997 operating income for the Delhi Group totaled $3.7 million, compared to $3.4 million in second quarter 1996. Excluding the first quarter portion of the pretax depreciation adjustment of $1.7 million, operating income for the 1997 period was $1.4 million lower than 1996, due to higher operating costs and lower total gross margins.
Delhi said its natural gas sales and trading margin decreased $1.8 million from 1996's second quarter primarily due to lower unit margins on increased gas sales volumes.

Transportation margin increased $0.8 million from 1996 due to a 25 percent increase in transportation volumes. Gathering service fees from treating, dehydration, compression and other services increased $1.1 million due to higher gas prices and increased transportation volumes.
